heroHeadline: Ceasefire Day 2: Russia Strikes Kharkiv Apartment, 8 Wounded — Putin Offers Zelenskyy Meeting Only After Peace Treaty
heroSubtitle: On May 10, the second day of the Trump-brokered 3-day ceasefire (May 9–11), Russia struck a 9-story residential building in Kharkiv's Industrial district with a drone — wounding 8 civilians including 2 children. Ukraine's Air Force intercepted all 27 drones Russia launched overnight from Primorsko-Akhtarsk and Millerovo, but one penetrated air defenses and hit the apartment. Across Ukraine, Russian forces continued 121+ combat clashes in all frontline directions; 1 civilian was killed in Zaporizhzhia Oblast and 19+ injured nationwide. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached 1,341,110 per the Ukrainian General Staff. Putin claimed the war is 'coming to an end' and offered to meet Zelenskyy in a neutral country — but only after a peace treaty is finalized, not during negotiations. The Kremlin conditioned talks on Ukrainian withdrawal from parts of Donetsk; Ukraine rejected this. US President Trump said he hoped for 'a big extension' of the ceasefire: 'It could be.' Zelenskyy pledged Ukraine would 'strictly mirror' Russian actions. Hungary's new government signaled it will end its EU aid veto, potentially unlocking the €90 billion loan to Kyiv that had been stalled.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Euronews, NPR, CBC, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
